title: Specialization homomorphism of abelian etale stalks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and $F$ an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Let $g:S_{(\bar s)}\to S$ be the structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] of the strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S_{(\bar s)}$ any geometric point. Define $\operatorname{sp}_{F,\bar s,\bar t}:F_{\bar s}\to F_{g\bar t}$, with stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], as the canonical restriction $r_F:F_{\bar s}\to\Gamma(S_{(\bar s)},g^{-1}F)$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-restriction], followed by the global-section germ at $\bar t$ and the canonical inverse-image stalk isomorphism $(g^{-1}F)_{\bar t}\cong F_{g\bar t}$, where inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Equivalently, a germ represented by $(U,\bar u,a)$ is sent to $(U,\bar v,a)$, where $\bar v$ is obtained by composing $\bar t$ with the canonical strict-local map to the pointed neighbourhood $U$. No algebraicity assumption on the test geometric point is imposed.
